notes: The first pose paint came back with the coloured skeleton drawn into the picture, and the reason is a naming trap. ComfyUI's union-type node names its modes after a different union model and passes the index straight through; on this FLUX Union-Pro the indices mean canny, tile, depth, blur, pose, gray and low-quality, so asking for "openpose" sent index 0, which is canny, and the GPU faithfully reproduced the sticks as edges. Pose is index 4, which ComfyUI calls "normal", and that is what is sent now. Because the number is what matters, the Photo Lab shows the mode under the pose grip with each index labelled by what this ControlNet actually does with it, so it can be switched without a new build if a ControlNet ever disagrees; the setting is shared with chat photos and the log line names it. The skeleton was also drawn far too thick, in the editor and in what the GPU received; it now follows the OpenPose convention, four pixels at 512 and scaled from there.
